p.src: When the company saw Ping’er arrive, they all asked, “What is your mistress doing? Why hasn’t she come?” Ping’er laughed. “How could she possibly find the time to come? She said she had scarcely had a chance to eat any and could not come herself, so she sent me to ask whether there were any left and, if so, to take a few home for her.” Xiangyun said, “Yes, there are plenty.” She promptly had ten of the largest brought over. “Give me a few more females with rounded bellies,” said Ping’er. The others tried to pull Ping’er down to sit with them, but she declined. Li Wan took hold of her and said with a laugh, “But I insist that you sit.” She drew Ping’er down beside her, raised a cup of wine, and held it to her lips. Ping’er hurriedly took a sip and made to leave. “I simply won’t allow you to go,” said Li Wan. It is plain that Feng is the only mistress you acknowledge—you no longer heed anything I say.” Then she ordered the matrons, “Take the box over first and tell her that I am keeping Ping’er here.” Before long, the old servant returned with the box and said, “Second Mistress asks that you ladies and young misses not laugh at her for begging delicacies. Inside this box are water-chestnut-flour cakes and chicken-fat rolls just sent over by the wife of the young ladies’ maternal uncle, for you ladies and young misses to enjoy.” Then she said to Ping’er, “She says that the moment she sends you here, you become so absorbed in the fun that you never come back. She advises you to drink a little less.” Ping’er laughed. “And what could she do to me if I drank too much?” As she spoke, she went on drinking freely and eating crab as well. Li Wan put an arm around her and said with a laugh, “What a pity that a girl with such fine looks and bearing should have so ordinary a fate and be left merely to serve in the inner rooms. Anyone who did not know you would surely take you for a lady of the household.”

p.src: As Ping’er ate and drank with Baochai, Xiangyun, and the others, she turned and said with a laugh, “My lady, please stop touching me like that—it tickles terribly.” “Oh!” exclaimed Li Wan. “What is this hard thing?” “Keys,” said Ping’er. “What keys?” asked Li Wan. “Are they for some precious private belongings that you fear might be stolen, so you must carry them on your person? I am always joking that when the Tang Monk journeyed for the scriptures, there was a white horse to carry him; when Liu Zhiyuan fought for the realm, there was a melon spirit to bring him armor; and where there is Feng, there is you. You are your mistress’s master key, so what need have you of these keys?” Ping’er laughed. “You have had some wine, my lady, and now you are making me the butt of your jokes again.” “But it is true,” Baochai said with a smile. Whenever we have nothing to do and begin discussing people, we always say that not one in a hundred could equal you few girls; best of all, each of you has virtues of her own.” Li Wan said, “In matters great and small, Heaven arranges things justly. Take the Old Lady’s apartments: how could they manage without Yuanyang? Beginning with Lady Wang herself, who else dares refuse a request from the Old Lady? Yet Yuanyang dares do so. And the Old Lady listens to her alone. No one else remembers all the Old Lady’s clothes and ornaments, but she remembers every one. If she did not manage them, there is no telling how much would be swindled away. The girl is fair-minded too. Despite her influence, she often speaks up for others and never uses her position to bully anyone.” Xichun laughed. “Only yesterday the Old Lady said that Yuanyang was more capable than any of us.” “She truly is a fine one,” said Ping’er. “How could we compare with her?” Baoyu said, “Caixia in Lady Wang’s apartments is an honest girl.” “Indeed she is,” said Tanchun. “She seems simple and honest outwardly, but she understands everything. Lady Wang is as serene as a Buddha and pays little attention to practical affairs, but Caixia knows all about them. In every sort of matter, she is the one who reminds Lady Wang what must be done. She even knows every important and trivial matter concerning the Master, whether he is at home or away. Whenever Lady Wang forgets something, Caixia privately reminds her.” “She does well enough,” said Li Wan. Pointing to Baoyu, she continued, “But if this young master’s apartments did not have Xiren, just imagine what a state they would be in! Even if Feng were Xiang Yu, the Hegemon-King of Chu, she would still need these two strong arms to lift a thousand-jin cauldron. If not for this girl, how could she possibly manage everything so thoroughly?” Ping’er laughed. “At first four maidservants accompanied her when she married, but some died and others left, until only I, a lonely ghost, remain.” Li Wan said, “You have been fortunate. Feng has been fortunate too. When your Master Zhu was alive, surely I too had a couple of such women.

p.src: Do you think I was the sort who could not tolerate them? Yet every day I saw how unhappy the two of them were. So as soon as your Master Zhu died, I released them both while they were still young. Had either one been willing to remain faithful and stay, I would have had a helping hand.” As she spoke, tears fell from her eyes. They all said, “Why grieve over it now? It was better to let them go.” With that, they all washed their hands and agreed to go together to pay their respects to the Lady Dowager and Lady Wang.

p.src: The old serving women and maids swept the pavilion and cleared away the cups and dishes. Xiren and Pinger went back together, and Xiren invited Pinger to sit awhile in her room and have another cup of tea. “No more tea,” said Pinger. “I will come again another time.” With that, she made to leave. Xiren called her back and asked, “Why has this month’s allowance not yet been paid, even to the Old Lady and Lady Wang?” At the question, Pinger quickly turned back to Xiren. Only after making sure that no one was nearby did she whisper, “You had better not ask. It will be paid in a few days anyway.” Xiren laughed. “What is the matter? Why are you so frightened?” Pinger confided in her in a whisper, “Our mistress drew this month’s allowance out long ago and lent it at interest. She will not pay it until the interest from her other loans comes in and she can make up the full amount. I am telling you only because it is you. You must not breathe a word of it to anyone.” “Can she possibly be short of money?” said Xiren. “Will she never have enough? Why burden herself with such schemes?” “That is exactly what I say,” Pinger replied with a laugh. Over the past few years, she has made several hundred taels by turning over this fund. She has no need to spend her official monthly allowance either, so whenever ten or eight taels accumulate, she lends them out. The interest on this private money alone comes to more than a thousand taels a year.” Xiren laughed. “So mistress and maid make interest with our money while keeping us poor fools waiting.” “How heartless of you to say that,” replied Pinger. Surely you are not short of spending money?” “I have no shortage,” said Xiren, “but I have nowhere else to spend it. I am saving it all for that one of ours.” Pinger said, “If anything urgent comes up and you need money, I still have a few taels. Take them and use them first, and tomorrow I will simply deduct the sum from your allowance.” “I do not need it just now,” said Xiren. “I only fear that if a sudden need arises, what I have may not suffice. In that case, I will send someone to fetch it.”

p.src: Pinger acknowledged this and went straight out through the garden gate to the main residence, where she found that Xifeng was not in her room. Then she noticed that Granny Liu, who had come to seek help on the previous occasion, had returned with Ban’er. They were sitting in the room opposite, attended by the wives of Zhang Cai and Zhou Rui, while two or three maids emptied dates, squashes, and wild greens from sacks onto the floor. When they saw Pinger enter, they all rose hastily. Having visited before, Granny Liu knew Pinger’s standing. She hurriedly jumped down from the kang, greeted her with “I hope you are well, miss,” and added, “Everyone at home sends their respects. I have long meant to come and pay my respects to your mistress and visit you young ladies, but farm work kept us busy. This year, by good fortune, we harvested two extra piculs of grain, and our fruits and vegetables were plentiful too. These are the first of the crop. We did not dare sell them but saved the choicest ones for your mistress and you young ladies to taste. You young ladies must be weary of rare delicacies every day, so these rustic things may offer a change. They are only a poor family’s token of devotion.” “Thank you for taking so much trouble,” Pinger replied. She invited Granny Liu to sit again and sat down herself. She also invited Aunt Zhang and Dame Zhou to sit and ordered a young maid to pour tea. The wives of Zhou Rui and Zhang Cai laughed and said, “You have a rosy glow today, miss; even your eyes are red around the rims.” “Indeed I do,” Pinger said with a laugh. I had not intended to drink, but the Young Mistress and the young ladies seized me and would not stop pressing wine on me. I had no choice but to take two cups, and my face immediately turned red.” Zhang Cai’s wife laughed. “I would have liked a drink, but no one invited me. The next time someone invites you, miss, take me along.” At this, everyone laughed. Zhou Rui’s wife said, “I saw those crabs early this morning. There are only two or three to a catty, they are so large. There were three great baskets of them, so they must have weighed seventy or eighty catties.” Zhou Rui’s wife added, “Even so, I fear there would not be enough for everyone in the household, high and low.” “Of course there was not enough,” said Pinger. “Only those of some standing received a couple apiece. As for the rest of the crowd, some managed to get one and some did not.” Granny Liu said, “Crabs like those cost five candareens a catty this year. Ten catties make five mace; five times five makes two taels five mace, and three times five makes fifteen. Add the wine and dishes, and the whole feast must have cost more than twenty taels of silver. Merciful Buddha! What this one meal cost would keep country folk like us for a whole year.” Pinger then asked, “I suppose you have already seen our mistress?” “Yes,” replied Granny Liu. “She told us to wait.” As she spoke, she looked through the window at the sky and said, “It is getting very late. We had better go, or we may not get out of the city before the gates close, and then we shall be in a predicament.” “That is true,” said Zhou Rui’s wife. “I will go and see what can be done for you.”

p.src: She went straight off and did not return for quite some time. Then she came back smiling. “Your good fortune has come, Granny! You have won the favor of both those ladies.” Pinger and the others asked what had happened. Zhou Rui’s wife replied with a laugh, “Second Mistress is with the Old Lady. I quietly told Second Mistress, ‘Granny Liu wants to go home, because she fears that if it gets late, she will not make it out of the city.’ Second Mistress said, ‘She has come such a long way and carried all those heavy things here. If it grows late, she can stay the night and leave tomorrow.’ Does that not show that you have found favor with Second Mistress? That alone would have been enough, but as luck would have it, the Old Lady overheard and asked who Granny Liu was. Second Mistress explained everything to her. The Old Lady said, ‘I have just been wishing for an elderly person well versed in old tales to talk with. Ask her to come so that I may meet her.’ Is that not an utterly unexpected blessing from heaven?” With that, she urged Granny Liu to get down and come along. Granny Liu said, “How can I appear before her looking like this? Dear sister, please just tell her that I have gone.” “Go along quickly,” Pinger said. “It will be all right. Our Old Lady is kinder to the aged and the poor than anyone. She is not like those flighty, deceitful people who put on airs. I suppose you are timid. Dame Zhou and I will escort you there.” With that, she and Zhou Rui’s wife led Granny Liu toward Grandmother Jia’s quarters.

p.src: When the pageboys on duty at the second gate saw Ping’er come out, they all rose, and two of them ran up after her, calling, “Miss!” Ping’er asked, “What is it now?” The pageboy smiled. “It’s already getting late, and my mother is ill and waiting for me to fetch a doctor. Dear Miss, might I have half a day’s leave?” Ping’er said, “You are a fine lot! You must have arranged it among yourselves—one of you asks for leave every day. Instead of reporting to Mistress, you simply come and pester me. The other day Zhu’er went off, and Second Master happened to call for him. When he could not be found, I answered for it, and was even accused of showing him favoritism. And now you come asking today.” Mrs. Zhou said, “His mother truly is ill. Miss, answer for him this once and let him go.” Ping’er said, “Come back first thing tomorrow morning. Mind you, I shall need you. Do not sleep until the sun is scorching your backside before you turn up! While you are out, take a message to Wang’er. Tell him Mistress asks about the interest money still outstanding. If he does not hand it over tomorrow, Mistress will no longer want it; she may as well make him a gift of it altogether.” Overjoyed, the pageboy promised to do so and left.

p.src: Ping’er and the others came to Grandmother Jia’s rooms, where the young ladies of Prospect Garden were all attending upon her. When Granny Liu entered, she saw a room full of bejeweled and elegantly dressed beauties, blooming like flowers, and had no idea who any of them were. She saw an old lady reclining on a couch, while behind her sat a maid as beautiful as any fine lady, wrapped in gauze and silk, massaging her legs; Xifeng stood nearby, talking and laughing. Granny Liu knew at once that this was Grandmother Jia. She hurried forward with a deferential smile, curtsied several times, and said, “My respects to the venerable lady of great longevity.” Grandmother Jia leaned forward to return her greeting, then ordered Mrs. Zhou to bring her a chair. Ban’er was still shy of strangers and did not know how to offer his greetings. Grandmother Jia asked, “My dear old relation, how old are you this year?” Granny Liu hastily rose and replied, “I am seventy-five this year.” Grandmother Jia said to the others, “At such a great age, she is still so hale and hearty. She is several years older than I am. If I live to her age, goodness knows whether I shall be able to move at all.” Granny Liu smiled. “We were born to endure hardship, while Your Ladyship was born to enjoy good fortune. If we lived as you do, there would be no one to do the farmwork.” Grandmother Jia asked, “Are your eyes and teeth still sound?” “They are both still sound,” said Granny Liu. “Only this year, one of the molars on my left has become loose.” Grandmother Jia said, “I am old and no longer good for anything. My sight is dim, my ears are deaf, and my memory is gone. I cannot even remember old relations like you. When relations visit, I fear they will laugh at me, for I know how to do nothing. I merely eat a few bites of whatever I can chew, take a nap, and when I am bored, joke and play awhile with these grandsons and granddaughters of mine. That is all.” Granny Liu smiled. “Why, that is precisely Your Ladyship’s good fortune. We could not live like that even if we wished to.” Grandmother Jia said, “What good fortune? I am merely a useless old thing.” At this, everyone laughed. Grandmother Jia then smiled and said, “I just heard Feng say that you brought a great many melons and vegetables. I told her to have them prepared quickly, for I have been longing to eat melons and greens freshly picked from the earth. Those bought outside are not as tasty as the ones from your fields.” Granny Liu smiled. “They are only rustic things; their novelty is all they have to recommend them. For our part, we long to eat fish and meat, but simply cannot afford them.” Grandmother Jia continued, “Now that we have acknowledged our kinship today, do not leave empty-handed at once. If you do not find our home objectionable, stay for a day or two before you go. We too have a garden, and there is fruit in it. Tomorrow you must taste some and take some home; then you may truly say you have paid a visit to your relations.”

If I live to her age, goodness knows whether I shall be able to move at all.”
Granny Liu smiled. “We were born to endure hardship, while Your Ladyship was born to enjoy good fortune.
If we lived as you do, there would be no one to do the farmwork.”
Grandmother Jia asked, “Are your eyes and teeth still sound?”
“They are both still sound,” said Granny Liu. “Only this year, one of the molars on my left has become loose.”
Grandmother Jia said, “I am old and no longer good for anything. My sight is dim, my ears are deaf, and my memory is gone.
I cannot even remember old relations like you.

When relations visit, I fear they will laugh at me, for I know how to do nothing. I merely eat a few bites of whatever I can chew, take a nap, and when I am bored, joke and play awhile with these grandsons and granddaughters of mine. That is all.”
Granny Liu smiled. “Why, that is precisely Your Ladyship’s good fortune.
We could not live like that even if we wished to.”
Grandmother Jia said, “What good fortune? I am merely a useless old thing.”
At this, everyone laughed.

Grandmother Jia then smiled and said, “I just heard Feng say that you brought a great many melons and vegetables. I told her to have them prepared quickly, for I have been longing to eat melons and greens freshly picked from the earth.
Those bought outside are not as tasty as the ones from your fields.”
Granny Liu smiled. “They are only rustic things; their novelty is all they have to recommend them.
For our part, we long to eat fish and meat, but simply cannot afford them.”
Grandmother Jia continued, “Now that we have acknowledged our kinship today, do not leave empty-handed at once.
If you do not find our home objectionable, stay for a day or two before you go.
We too have a garden, and there is fruit in it. Tomorrow you must taste some and take some home; then you may truly say you have paid a visit to your relations.”

p.src: Seeing how pleased Grandmother Jia was, Xifeng also hurried to urge Granny Liu to stay. “Though our place is not as large as your threshing grounds, we still have a couple of empty rooms. Stay for two days and tell our old lady some of the news and stories from your part of the country.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “Feng, do not make fun of her. She is an honest countrywoman. How could she withstand your teasing?” As she spoke, she ordered someone to fetch a handful of fruit for Ban’er. But with so many people present, Ban’er did not dare eat it. Grandmother Jia then ordered that he be given some money and told the young attendants to take him outside to play. After drinking her tea, Granny Liu told Grandmother Jia about things she had seen and heard in the countryside, and Grandmother Jia found them more and more entertaining. While they were still talking, Xifeng sent someone to invite Granny Liu to supper. Grandmother Jia also selected several dishes from her own table and ordered that they be sent over for Granny Liu to eat.

p.src: Xifeng, knowing that this had pleased Grandmother Jia, sent Grannie Liu back after the meal. Yuanyang promptly told an old maidservant to take Grannie Liu for a bath, while she herself chose two ordinary garments and had her change into them. Grannie Liu had never encountered such treatment before. She hurriedly changed and came out, then sat before Grandmother Jia’s couch and searched her mind for more stories to tell. Baoyu and the girls were also sitting there at the time. Never having heard such tales, they found them even more entertaining than the stories told by blind storytellers. Though Grannie Liu was a rustic countrywoman, she possessed some native shrewdness; moreover, being advanced in years, she had seen much of the world. Seeing, first, how delighted Grandmother Jia was and, second, how eagerly the young masters and misses listened, she would invent stories to tell even when she had run out of real ones. She said, “In our village we till the fields and grow vegetables every day of every year, through spring, summer, autumn, and winter, in wind and rain. When do we ever have a moment to sit idle? We spend every day resting out by the fields, as though they were our wayside pavilion, so what manner of strange and curious things have we not seen? “Last winter, for instance, snow fell for several days on end and lay three or four feet deep upon the ground. “One morning I rose early and, before I had even left my room, heard the firewood rustling outside. “I thought someone must have come to steal our firewood. “But when I peered through a crack in the window, I saw that it was no one from our village.” “It must have been some travelers chilled by the road,” said Grandmother Jia. “Seeing firewood ready to hand, perhaps they pulled some out to make a warming fire.” Grannie Liu smiled. “It was no traveler either—that is what made it so strange. “Who do you suppose it was, venerable lady? “Why, it was an exceedingly pretty girl of seventeen or eighteen, her hair combed glossy and smooth, wearing a bright-red padded jacket and a white satin skirt…” She had only reached this point when a commotion suddenly arose outside and someone cried, “It is nothing serious! Do not alarm the old lady.” Grandmother Jia and the others anxiously asked what had happened. A maid replied, “The stables in the south courtyard caught fire, but it is nothing serious; the flames have already been brought under control.” Grandmother Jia was extremely timid. At these words she hurriedly rose, supported by attendants, and went out to the veranda to look. A glow from the fire could still be seen in the southeast. Terrified, Grandmother Jia murmured invocations to the Buddha and hastily ordered someone to burn incense before the God of Fire. Lady Wang and the others also hurried over to reassure her, reporting, “The fire is already out. Please go back inside, Old Lady.” Only after Grandmother Jia had watched the glow die away completely did she lead everyone back inside. Baoyu promptly asked Grannie Liu, “What was that girl doing pulling firewood out in all that snow? “What if she had caught ill from the cold?” “It was this talk of pulling out firewood that brought on a fire just now,” said Grandmother Jia. “And still you ask about it!

p.src: “Say no more about that. Tell us something else.” Though displeased at heart when he heard this, Baoyu had no choice but to let the matter drop. Grannie Liu thought up another tale and began, “In the village east of ours lives an old lady who is now more than ninety years of age. “Every day she ate vegetarian food and prayed to the Buddha, until at last she moved the Bodhisattva Guanyin, who appeared to her in a dream one night and said, ‘Because you are so devout, although your line was fated to die out, I have now petitioned the Jade Emperor to grant you a grandson.’ “This old lady had only one son, and that son in turn had only one son. After they had struggled to raise the boy to seventeen or eighteen, he died, and she wept as though her heart would break. “Sure enough, another boy was later born. He is only thirteen or fourteen this year, with skin as fair as a ball of snow, and is remarkably bright and clever. “That proves the gods and Buddhas truly exist.” This story accorded perfectly with the deepest hopes of Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang, and even Lady Wang became wholly absorbed in listening.

p.src: Baoyu could think of nothing but the story of the girl pulling out firewood, and brooded over it in gloomy silence. Tanchun asked him, “Yesterday we imposed on Cousin Shi. Why do we not go back and arrange another poetry gathering to return her hospitality, and invite the Old Lady to admire the chrysanthemums as well?” Baoyu smiled. “The Old Lady said she means to give a banquet in return for Cousin Shi’s and have us attend as her guests. “It will not be too late for us to invite her after we have attended the Old Lady’s banquet.” “It will only grow colder from now on,” said Tanchun. “The Old Lady may not be inclined to come.” “But the Old Lady likes rain and snow,” said Baoyu. “Why not wait for the first snowfall and invite her to admire the snow? Would that not be delightful? “Writing poems in the snow would be more enjoyable too.” Daiyu hastily laughed. “Writing poems in the snow? “In my opinion, it would be even more amusing to fetch a bundle of firewood and pull sticks out of it in the snow.” At this, Baochai and the others all laughed. Baoyu shot her a glance but made no reply.

p.src: When the gathering broke up, Baoyu secretly drew Granny Liu aside and questioned her closely about who the girl was. Granny Liu had no choice but to invent an answer: “She was originally enshrined in a little shrine beside the ridge north of our village. She wasn’t a deity or a Buddha; long ago there was some gentleman or other.” As she spoke, she tried to think of a name. Baoyu said, “The name doesn’t matter. Don’t trouble yourself to remember it; just tell me how it all came about.” Granny Liu said, “This gentleman had no sons, only one daughter, whose name was Mingyu. The young lady was well read and literate, and her parents treasured her like a precious jewel. Sadly, when Miss Mingyu reached the age of seventeen, she fell ill and died.” On hearing this, Baoyu stamped his foot and sighed with regret, then asked what happened afterward. Granny Liu said, “Because her father and mother could never cease longing for her, they built this shrine, made an image of Miss Mingyu, and appointed someone to tend the incense and the fire. But after so many years, the attendants are gone and the shrine has fallen into ruin, so that image has turned into a spirit.” Baoyu hastily said, “She hasn’t turned into a spirit. As a rule, a person like her does not truly die even after death.” Granny Liu said, “Amitabha Buddha! So that is how it is. If you hadn’t told me, young master, we would all have thought she had become a spirit. She often takes human form and wanders idly through the villages and along the roads by the inns. That is why I just said the girl gathering firewood must have been her. The people in our village were even discussing smashing the image and razing the shrine.” Baoyu hurriedly said, “You must not do that. If you raze the shrine, you will incur no small sin.” Granny Liu said, “Luckily you told me, young master. I shall tell them as soon as I return tomorrow.” Baoyu said, “Our Old Lady and Madam are both charitable people, and everyone in our household delights in doing good and giving alms. They especially love restoring temples and making sacred images. Tomorrow I shall draw up a subscription notice and collect some donations for you. You can become the shrine keeper, save the money to rebuild the shrine and refurbish the clay image, and I shall give you money each month for incense. Wouldn’t that be a fine arrangement?” Granny Liu said, “If that happens, I shall owe it to the young lady’s blessing that I too have a little money to spend.” Baoyu then asked her the names of the place and village, how far away they were, how one traveled there, and exactly where the shrine stood. Granny Liu glibly made it all up on the spot.

p.src: Baoyu believed every word. Returning to his room, he pondered the matter all night. Early the next morning, he came out and gave Mingyan several hundred cash. Following the directions and place-names Granny Liu had supplied, he ordered Mingyan to go and investigate everything clearly before they decided what to do. After Mingyan left, Baoyu waited and waited, but he did not return. Baoyu grew as frantic as an ant on a hot pan. Only after waiting with great difficulty until sunset did he finally see Mingyan return in high spirits. Baoyu hastily asked, “Was there a shrine?” Mingyan laughed. “You must have heard the directions incorrectly, Master. You gave me a fine search. The place-name and location were not as you described, so I searched all day. Only on a field ridge to the northeast did I finally find a ruined shrine.” At this news, Baoyu beamed with delight and quickly said, “Granny Liu is old; it is only natural that she might remember it wrongly for a moment. Just tell me what you saw.” Mingyan said, “The shrine door did indeed face south, and the place was badly dilapidated. I was thoroughly vexed from searching when I saw it, and I said, ‘At last!’ and hurried inside. But one look at the clay image frightened me so badly that I ran straight out. It looked exactly like a living creature.” Baoyu laughed delightedly. “Since she can assume human form, naturally she must possess some living vitality.” Mingyan clapped his hands. “There was no girl at all! It was a plague god with a blue-green face and red hair.” Baoyu spat in disgust and cursed him. “What a useless wretch you are! You cannot even manage such a trifling errand.” Mingyan said, “Second Master, who knows what book you have read or whose nonsense you have heard and taken for truth? You sent me off to blunder about on this senseless errand, so how can you call me useless?” Seeing that Mingyan was upset, Baoyu hurriedly soothed him. “Don’t be angry. When you have time another day, go and look again. If she deceived us, then naturally there will be nothing to find; but if the shrine truly exists, would you not be earning hidden merit as well? I shall reward you handsomely.” As they were speaking, a page from the inner gate came to report, “The maids from the Old Lady’s apartments are standing at the inner gate asking for Second Master.” To learn the full particulars, read the next chapter.
